Rashi on Pesachim 10b:11:1.hebrew: ככר בפי נחש - בעיא באנפי נפשה היא, ולא דמי להנך דלעיל, ול"ג את"ל:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:11:1.english: A loaf in the mouth of a snake - This is an independent dilemma and is not similar to those [cases] above, and we do not read: 'If you say.'

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:12:1.english: [The Sages] did not trouble him - And let him nullify [it] in his heart.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:12:2.english: With his money - To hire a snake charmer.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:14:1.hebrew: בתוך המועד - בשעה ששית, שהוא מועד הביעור:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:14:1.english: Within the appointed time - In the sixth hour, which is the appointed time of removal.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:14:2.english: After the appointed time - From the sixth hour and onward, until nightfall.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:15:1.hebrew: שלש השבתות - שלש לשונות של השבתה — ראייה, מציאה, והשבתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:15:1.english: Three removals - Three expressions of removal: seeing, finding, and removal.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:16:1.hebrew: אלמא במכאן ואילך הוא דפליגי - ולאו במידי אחרינא, דר' יהודה לא מצריך שלש בדיקות, אלא הכי קאמר: או אור לארבעה עשר, או שחרית, או בשעה ששית. ורבנן אמרי: אם לא בדק בתוך המועד — יבדוק לאחריו:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:16:1.english: Evidently, it is from this point forward that they disagree - And not regarding anything else, for Rabbi Yehuda does not require three searches; rather, this is what he is saying: Either the evening of the fourteenth, or morning, or in the sixth hour. And the Rabbis say: If he did not search during the appointed time, he should search after it.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:17:1.english: And Mar Zutra taught - Explicitly: “At one of three times.”

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:19:1.hebrew: לבתר איסורא - לא יבדוק, דגזרינן דילמא איידי דעסיק ביה, אתי למיכל מיניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:19:1.english: After the prohibition - He should not search, for we decree lest, since he is occupied with it, he come to eat from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:1:1.hebrew: הבית טמא - כל כלי הבית טמאין, שאני אומר: אדם טמא נכנס לשם ומשמש בכל כלי הבית:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:1:1.english: The house is impure - All the vessels of the house are impure, as I say: An impure person entered there and handled all the vessels of the house.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:20:1.hebrew: משקרב העומר - בו ביום יוצאים ומוצאים שוקי ירושלים מלאים קמח וקלי מן החדש למכור, וקודם י"ט נקטף ונטחן, ונתייבש הקלי בתנור:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:20:1.english: Once the Omer was sacrificed - On that very day, [people] would go out and find the markets of Jerusalem filled with flour and toasted grain from the new [crop] for sale; and prior to the Festival, [the grain] was harvested and ground, and the toasted grain was dried in an oven.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:2:1.hebrew: זוית מאן דכר שמיה - פתח באבדו, וסיים בנמצא בזוית אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:2:1.english: A corner, who mentioned anything about it? - [The baraita] began with its being lost, and concluded with [its] being found in another corner.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:3:1.hebrew: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני - שאני אומר: אדם טמא נכנס לשם ולקחו — לאבוד; וגבי מצא בזוית אחרת — שמא אדם טמא הניחו שם. רבן שמעון כו'. וגבי חמץ נמי: לרבנן, חוששין שמא עכבר עשה, וכיון דחוששין לעכבר — יש לחוש נמי: לא זהו, אלא אחר; ולרבן שמעון, תולין באדם עצמו שהוא עשה ושכח, וא"צ בדיקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:3:1.english: It is incomplete, and is teaching the following - “As I say: An impure person entered there and took it” — [this applies] to [the case of an axe being] lost; and regarding [the case where he] found [it] in another corner — lest an impure person placed it there. “Rabban Shimon,” etc. And regarding leaven as well: according to the Rabbis, we are concerned lest a mouse did [it], and since we are concerned for a mouse, there is concern as well [that] this is not that [one], but another [one]; while according to Rabban Shimon, we attribute [it] to the person himself, that he did [it] and forgot, and [the house] does not require a search.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:4:1.hebrew: ונכנס אחריו ומצא פירורין צריך בדיקה - ואין תולין הככר בו, שאין דרכו של עכבר לפרר, ולא זהו ככר שהכניס העכבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:4:1.english: And he entered after it and found crumbs, [it] requires searching - And we do not attribute the loaf to it, for it is not the way of a mouse to crumble [bread], and this is not the loaf that the mouse brought in.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:6:1.hebrew: אם תמצא לומר היינו האי כו' - דאי פשטת ליה דחיישינן דילמא אחרינא הואי, תו לא צריכנא למיבעי שחור ולבן. אבל אי פשטת ליה דלא חיישינן, אכתי שחור ולבן מיבעיא לן:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:6:1.english: If you say this is that [same mouse], etc. - For if you resolve it that we are concerned lest it was a different [mouse], we would no longer need to ask [about] a black and a white [mouse]. But if you resolve it that we are not concerned, [the case of] a black and a white [mouse] is still a dilemma for us.

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:6:2.hebrew: ארמוייה - השליכו ממנו ונטלו הוא. וחבירו בחגיגה (ד' טו:): ״אי נקטיה ביד, מאן מרמי ליה מן ידי״:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:6:2.english: He cast it down - He knocked it away from him and took it himself. And its parallel appears in Chagigah (15b): “If I take him by the hand, who can cast him down from my hand?”

Rashi on Pesachim 10b:8:1.hebrew: ככר ועכבר בפי חולדה - עכבר נכנס וככר בפיו, וחולדה יוצא' כשנכנס בו לבדוק, ובפיה ככר מכאן ועכבר מכאן:
Rashi on Pesachim 10b:8:1.english: A loaf and a mouse in the mouth of a marten - A mouse entered with a loaf in its mouth, and a marten was coming out when he entered it to search, and in its mouth were a loaf on this side and a mouse on that side.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:12:1.hebrew: בממוניה לא אטרחוהו רבנן - פי': הכא דוק', דשמא יוציאנה או יאכלנה; אבל היכא דאיכא חמץ, אמר לעיל (פסחים דף ד:) דניחא ליה לאינש דליעבד מצוה בממוניה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:12:1.english: "With regard to his money, the Sages did not obligate him to exert himself" - Explanation: [This applies] specifically here, for perhaps [the snake] will take it out or eat it; but where there is [definitely] leaven, [the Gemara] said above (Pesachim 4b) that a person is pleased to perform a mitzvah with his money.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:14:1.hebrew: ואם לא בדק בתוך המועד - פי' הקונטרס: בשעה ששית. וקשה: דלרבי יהודה קרי ליה "שעת הביעור", ולמה שינה לשונו? אלא "בתוך המועד" — היינו מתחלת שבע עד סוף הפסח, "ולאחר המועד יבדוק" — כדי שלא יתערב לו חמץ של איסור בשל היתר ויאכלנו. ורש"י לא רצה לפרש כן, מפני שפירש במשנה דבודקים שלא יעבור בבל יראה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:14:1.english: "And if he did not search during the Festival" - The Kunteres explains: In the sixth hour. And this is difficult: for regarding Rabbi Yehuda, it calls it "the time of removal"; why then did it change its phrasing? Rather, "during the Festival" means from the beginning of the seventh [hour] until the end of Passover; and "he should search after the Festival" is so that forbidden leaven does not become mixed with permitted [food] for him and he eat it. And Rashi did not wish to explain this way because he explained on the Mishnah that one searches so that one does not violate [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen."

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:1:1.hebrew: הניח בזוית זו ומצא בזוית אחרת פלוגתא דרבן שמעון בן גמליאל ורבנן - דלרבנן צריך בדיקה, דחוששין שמא עכבר עשה ולא זהו שהניח; ולית להו לרבנן "הוא שאבד הוא שנמצא", אלא כרשב"ג, דאמר: "תיבדק כל השדה כולה". אי נמי, אתי אפי' כר', ומיירי כגון שאין יודע כמה ככרות הניח, וצריך בדיקה שמא לא מצא כולם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:1:1.english: "[If] one placed in this corner and found in another corner, [this is] the dispute of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis" - For according to the Rabbis, a search is required, as we suspect that perhaps a mouse did [this] and this is not that which he placed; and the Rabbis do not hold [the principle that] "what was lost is what was found," but rather [hold] like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said: "Let the entire field be searched." Alternatively, [this] can follow even Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and it is dealing [with a case] where he does not know how many loaves he placed, and a search is required lest he did not find all of them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:1:2.hebrew: שאני אומר אדם טמא נכנס לשם - וא"ת: דהכא ובפרק קמא דחולין (דף ט:) גבי צלוחית תלינן באדם טמא, ובפרק קמא דנדה (דף ד.) גבי ככר הנתון על גבי הדף ומדף טמא מונח תחתיה תלינן באדם טהור? ותירץ ר"ת: דאמר בפ"ק דשבת (דף טו:) גזרו על ספק כלים הנמצאים, ולא גזרו על ספק אוכלין הנמצאים. אי נמי: גבי ככר, רגלים לדבר שטהור הסירו — שלא יפול על המדף ויטמא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:1:2.english: "For I say an impure person entered there" - And if you say: Here, and in the first chapter of Chullin (9b) regarding a flask, we assume [it was taken by] an impure person; whereas in the first chapter of Niddah (4a) regarding a loaf placed upon a board with an impure shelf lying beneath it, we assume [it was taken by] a pure person? And Rabbeinu Tam answered: As [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Shabbat (15b), they decreed [impurity] on found vessels of uncertain status, but they did not decree on found food of uncertain status. Alternatively: In the case of the loaf, there are grounds [to assume] that a pure person removed it, so that it would not fall upon the shelf and become impure.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:4:1.hebrew: מפני שדרכו של תינוק לפרר - ומיירי שיש פירורין כדי כל הככר, ולכך אין צריך בדיקה. ואפי' לרבן שמעון בן גמליאל דאמר "תיבדק כל השדה כולה" — הכא רגלים לדבר יש שהפרורים מן הככר, שהרי מיד נכנס אחריו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:4:1.english: "Because a child typically generates crumbs" - And [this] is dealing with [a case where] there are crumbs equivalent to the entire loaf, and therefore it does not require searching. And even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who says, "The entire field must be examined," here there is circumstantial evidence that the crumbs are from the loaf, since he entered immediately after him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:5:1.hebrew: מי אמרינן היינו הא דעל היינו הא דנפק - ואפילו לרשב"ג, דאמר "תיבדק כל השדה כולה" — הכא רגלים לדבר, שהרי הוא עם הככר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:5:1.english: "Do we say: This is the one that entered, [and] this is the one that left" - And [this applies] even according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said, "Let the entire field be searched" — [for] here there is circumstantial evidence, since it is with the loaf.

Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:5:2.hebrew: או דילמא אחרינא הוא - ואפי' לר', דאמר "הוא שנמצא הוא שנאבד", הכא חיישינן — דמסתמא הראשונה נשאר בבית, וזהו אחר שיצא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 10b:5:2.english: "Or perhaps it is a different [mouse]" - And even according to Rabbi, who says, "That which was found is that which was lost," here we are concerned — for presumably the first [one] remained in the house, and this is another [one] that left.
